sourceIdentity.counting_rule: One K6 candidate; K10, language editions and administration modes are not counted as additional instruments.
sourceIdentity.selected_version: Six scored K6 symptom questions Q1a–f, extracted verbatim from official K6+ self-report form; past30days. Not an entire reproduction of all K6+ supplementary questions.
sourceIdentity.primary_language_candidate: Official author-hosted Mandarin translation (2006 copyright notice); original English retained for verification.
sourceIdentity.population_scope: Adult first-review scope. No youth validity or universal Chinese norms inferred.
sourceIdentity.version_lock: Retain 30-day frame, exact six stems and frequency labels. Do not substitute worst-month-in-past-year or7-day questions without a separate version/evidence review.

originalPapersLinkOnly.citation: Kessler RC et al. Screening for serious mental illness in the general population. Archives of General Psychiatry.2003;60(2):184–189.
originalPapersLinkOnly.access_status: Publisher full article readable through web; author copy indexed but direct fetch timed out. No article PDF copied.
originalPapersLinkOnly.summary: Enriched convenience sample155; reference12-month DSM-IV disorder (excluding substance-use disorder) with GAF<60. Cutoff13+ on0–24 equalized weighted false positives/negatives; sensitivity.36, specificity.96. Critically, NHSDA implementation changed recall to the emotionally worst month within the previous12months. These performance estimates must not be presented as validation of the selected30-day Mandarin form.

chineseValidationEvidence.citation: Kang YK et al. The6-item Kessler psychological distress scale to survey serious mental illness among Chinese undergraduates: Psychometric properties and prevalence estimate. Comprehensive Psychiatry.2015;63:105–112.
chineseValidationEvidence.population: 8,289 randomly sampled students at one major comprehensive Chinese university;222 reassessed/interviewed using Chinese CIDI3.1.
chineseValidationEvidence.caveat: Primary abstract evidence only; exact Chinese wording, translator lineage, recall and scoring implementation need full-text/version matching. Not national norms and not proof for all ages or Mandarin-speaking populations.

chineseValidationEvidence.citation: Lee et al. Performance of the6-item Kessler scale for measuring serious mental illness in Hong Kong. Comprehensive Psychiatry.2012;53(5):584–592.
chineseValidationEvidence.population: Hong Kong telephone population survey3,014;153 clinician reassessments.
chineseValidationEvidence.reliability: Abstract reports high internal consistency and test-retest reliability; coefficients not independently extracted.
chineseValidationEvidence.caveat: Cantonese/Hong Kong context is not a validation of the author-posted Mandarin translation; no Hong Kong prevalence or individual probability transplanted into reports.

originalEnglishThresholdsReviewOnly.interpretation_policy: No mild/moderate/severe bands or percentile norms approved. Display continuous0–24 descriptive distress score only pending independent review; any future threshold display must name applicable population, period, language and source.
originalEnglishThresholdsReviewOnly.prevalence_warning: Do not estimate SMI prevalence as raw percentage scoring13+ in arbitrary sample; official scoring FAQ warns calibration depends on population characteristics.

scope: Six Q1a–f symptoms only, not complete K6+. No added attention or safety item. No article PDFs, app registration, deployment or human review claim. Current 30-day Mandarin report has no automatic threshold/band.
